core_obligations: Reduce to the strictly henselian case (proof lines 19484-19490): as in the proof of the beta lemma one may replace S by Spec(O^sh_{S,s}), after which the maps simplify to h : X_t -> X, i : X_s -> X and beta_{K,s,t} : K -> Rh_*(K|_{X_t}).

Compute the composite (proof lines 19491-19498): using (Rf_*K)_s = R Gamma(X, K), the composite of sp with the base change map (Rf_*K)_t -> R Gamma(X_t, K) is the pullback of cohomology along h, which coincides with the map R Gamma(X, K) -> R Gamma(X, Rh_*(K|_{X_t})) = R Gamma(X_t, K) induced by beta.

Conclude commutativity (proof lines 19499-19504): the map cosp first inverts the identification in the displayed formula and then applies the same map, so the two ways around the square agree, which is the commutativity asserted.
proof_roadmap: Base change to the strict henselisation so that the three maps take their simplified form.
Identify the composite of sp with the base change map as the map induced by beta on cohomology.
Observe that cosp inverts the displayed identification and applies the same map, giving commutativity.
difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the commutativity of the square relating the specialization and cospecialization maps (statement lines 19468-19481). The proof (proof lines 19483-19504) reduces to the strictly henselian case, where the maps simplify, identifies the composite of sp with the base change map as the map induced by beta on cohomology using the description of the stalk of the pushforward, and reads off the commutativity since cosp inverts the same identification. H2: one reduction and one identification, written out.
